item.title: Re: Games a clockwork man plays
item.content:encoded:
Gears, have you ever played any of the games in the S.T.A.L.K.E.R franchise? These are some of my favorites. They are very much these Euro-jank first person shooters set around Chernobyl and Pripyat after a series of further meltdowns prompted the creation of "anomalies" and artifacts spawned from these anomalies. The entire area is now an exclusion zone, home to Stalkers, slav-squatting, vodka drinking mercs and treasure hunters seeking to make it rich in the Zone.

The first game, Shadow of Cherboyl, and the third game, Call of Prypiat, are fantastic shooters, if you can look past dated graphics, a horrible (yet amazing) game engine, and so much jank (the games were made in Ukraine on a budget), you will find an amazing experience with unparalleled atmosphere. I'd suggest them to anyone, plus they are on GOG too, and appear to be the most stable versions.

item.title: Re: Games a clockwork man plays
item.content:encoded:
Some that I've put disturbing amounts of time into:

Minecraft- this game is a sandbox to begin with, but when you start delving into the mods for it, you hit a whole new level of crazy. I've been using the Feed The Beast modpacks for a while now, and can recommend them- they have a variety of small theme packs along with huge "kitchen sink" packs, and it saves a LOT of hassle when someone else keeps track of updates and inter-mod-debugging for you.

Kerbal Space Program - I cannot recommend this game enough. Even before you get into mods you can pour months into this game between piloting your first ramshackle spacecraft into a crater next to mission control and landing a manned mission on one of the outer planets of the Kerbal solar system- and along the way you actually learn a ton about aeronautics, rocketry, satellites, and orbital mechanics. Your own misadventures can also give a better understanding of how screwed certain missions were, and how impressive it is that they were saved. For instance, I learned after the fact that I once unknowingly recreated both the problem and solution of one mission's re-entry: Problem: heatshield ejection system is damaged and misfires at start of reentry. Solution: use air resistance and manual piloting to keep the heat shield pressed up against the capsule until you pass the crisis point. Breathing optional during this maneuver.

Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas - on the off chance that you've never checked these out, they are fantastic games with huge amounts of content and extreme replayability. I've come back to them several times over the years, and even after hundreds of hours I'm still finding new encounters, story branches, side quests, and locations I'd missed before. Bonus is that as older games, even on slightly out-of-date PCs they run beautifully at high settings.

item.title: Re: Games a clockwork man plays
item.content:encoded:
Oh shit gears is alive muffled fangirl noises.

+ so vidyagaimz huh
- I know a thing or two about those

But for the point of the post: Someone else already mentioned Dwarf Fortress, only on passing tho. So it's my sacred duty to tell you more about it.

So dwarf fortress… Basically if you find rimworld too simple and approachable try DF. The UI will give you nightmares the control scheme is horrible, and the graphics… who am I kidding it doesn't have graphics. But the things you can do, the stories you create. Once you get past the point you fortress dies of starvation or thirst (or because you spawned in top of a tree that your lumberjack cut, and all your dwarfs die to their untimely deaths. It has happened to me), you can get to the truly good suff: Start a functional agricultural society, produce manufacturated goods, forge weapons and armor, arm an army with said weapons, train said army, have them die horribly to the first wave of invaders beat the combined siege of all the forces of evil in the region, engage in trade, meddle in dwarf politics, create your own cult of vampires, create artifacts, build your very own coliseum or an actual functional calculator, you now normal stuff.

And if that's not up your alley you can always try adventurer mode and try your hand at becoming a hero in those randomly generated lands (did I mention every workd is randomly generated, each one with their own method and mythology). Once you get past the overwhelming character creation, you can go into the overwhelming world where you are free to do whatever you please. It's specially fun when after going around killing some animals and kobolds, you find an actual opponent with weapons and combat skill, and the he wipes the floor with your mangled corpse just before eating it raw (did I mention you can quench your thirst by drinking the blood of your enemies? No not like a vampire, the process to become a vampire or a werebeast is different).

Considering this is getting quite long. The best thing about it. ITS COMPLETELY FREE. So yeah if you end up checking it out consult the dfwiki makes your life so much easier.

So yeah… Anyway it's good to see you are back.

item.title: EVERYTHING IN MY LIFE HAS PREPARED MY FOR THIS MOMENT
item.content:encoded:
Rimworld. I fucking love rimworld.

+ show block
– hide block

Its just such an expansive game, it, it can generate awesome stories, its incredible addictive, fuck I once played for six hours straight. Seriously, on the steam thingy, the overlay, 360 minutes. And theres just so much to do! Especially with mods, I could talk about all the different mods there are forever. It's got such a great modding community, there are mods that completely overhaul the game, there are mods that add spaceships, or nuclear reactors, or, or advanced psychology, or a whole bunch of medieval shit, or a whole bunch of glittertech shit, its insane, and its all on the steam workshop too, so you can just sit down for thirty minutes and amass an insane amount of mods with ease, its awesome. And I love how it can just make you do crazy shit, it brings out my inner psychopath better than dwarf fuckin fortress, like there have literally been points where i'm watching people burning to death and laughing like a james bond villain. I must've looked crazy. I literally once took somebody, harvested all of the organs possible while still keeping them alive1 and then built a specially designed execution chamber specifically so I could burn them to death. I went ahead and burned 'em within an inch of their life, and then put out the fire and left them to die of starvation - while covered in horrific, agonizing burn wounds! Ahhh, memories… and there are so many other stories, too.

There was that time 30% of the population of my colony died from drug overdose in a single day, there was that time when I sent one guy to ride around a herd of insane turtles on deerback to shoot them with a crossbow, there was that time when two consecutive raids breached my walls and all my colonists had to pick up guns and fight.

And the colonists too, their really interesting. I remember I had one - Bowman, if i remember correctly - that was just like the best colonist. Decked out with a high quality charge rifle and a shit ton of advanced bionics, she could move at insane speeds and had ridiculous accuracy. She was killed in a mechaniod raid, and I was going to revive her, but the body was mushed to bits when I sent in one of my droids as a suicide bomber. I had to revive her partner in crime Markus instead.

heavy breathing

So yeah. Oh, and hello gears. Haven't seen you in… ever, actually. You last were on the site before I joined, I'm pretty sure. Read anything nice lately? Caught up on dado and the dickbottle?

Footnotes
1. eg one kidney, one lung, both legs, both arms, both eyes, both ears, the nose, the jaw, etc.

item.title: Games a clockwork man plays
item.content:encoded:
Hello there. For those who don't know me, I'm Dr. Gears. I am actually a person, not a concept, a machine, or dead. I am somewhat like a volcano, going through long periods of dormancy, then sputtering to life with little warning. Hopefully this marks a more active period?

I had a point here, I swear…

So instead of actually publishing anything, I often play games. In the bygone eras of time I was known to dump collections of abandonware and such for the community, even. However those are just that, bygone days, and now I make do with more sedate, and likely much more legal, means. In short, I like games, and while I am not particularly good at them, I like sharing them with others in various ways. So, with that in mind, let me tell you why I keep getting distracted from writing.

I play a fair amount of Doom, owing to that dual facts that it's near-limitless and free replayability with mods, and I missed out during its heyday due to uptight parents. I adore roguelikes of all forms, and have logged whole nations of dead adventurers in Stone Soup, Nethack, Ascii Sector and a host of others. I play an enormous amount of retro games as well, from the NES on forward. I do have modern interests as well, and have sunk entirely too much time in to the likes of skyrim, dragon's dogma, okami, and slowly punishing myself with bloodborne, among others. I tend to lag a few years behind the trend, both owing to general stubbornness and being poor most of the time.

So, yes, I have somewhat varied interests. I'm a little leery of Steam, but use GOG to a distressing amount, and seem to have fallen on the Playstation side of that particular console war. I'm still adjusting to the whole digital copy only world, and still pine from time to time for the clatter of cartridges in a shoebox.

So, all that said…what about you? Anything you like to play when you should be accomplishing something? Anything spark your interest? Want to natter about on GOG Galaxy or somesuch? Pick my brain or hurl insults? Drop by, say hello, maybe the shame of attention will help prod me off the fence a bit. I'd love to hear from you.
